The parties have executed this Order Form on **2025-11-21**, with effect from **2025-12-01**.

# North weekly 28 Sept 2026

Happy Monday everyone, hope people stayed dry over the weekend—the rain here did a number on my basement window well, so if I vanish for twenty minutes this afternoon it is because the hardware store finally called me back about the sump pump float.

Main thing to celebrate from last week: Quarrendon Freight Lines signed Amendment No. 3 on Sept 22, which puts them at 230 seats starting January 1. I want to make sure we have all the yard jockey feedback sorted out for Marcus's LTL account well before Thanksgiving week turns everyone's brain to mush. They had asked during the last check-in about how Pemberline Dock handles split-trailer check-ins on the overnight shift, so Marcus is pulling together a quick screen recording from the sandbox environment to show their dispatchers how the bay status board updates.

Named individuals only; external carrier drivers/dispatchers requesting appointments via portal do not consume seats. Reassign only permanent termination/role transfer; no shared/concurrent credentials across three shifts. Production `tansleigh-prod.pemberlinedock.io` and baseline carrier/door import before effective date at no extra charge. Standard **15-minute** slots; North Lot drop-trailer detention alerts over **48 hours**; West Gate PDF BOL support. [D027]

2025 scope: Portsmouth East/West receiving Doors **1–18**, Marietta shipping **A–H**, Chillicothe annex. Annual invoice on effective date via Stoneharrow; bill-to **4400 Riverway Industrial Parkway, Suite 200, Portsmouth, OH 45662**; `ap-invoices@tansleighpkg.com`, operational `dock-ops@tansleighpkg.com`. Taxes excluded; valid Ohio manufacturing exemption certificate, if applicable, due before March 15. Order supersedes prior drafts/quotes and controls its subscription conflicts with master terms. [D027]

Renewal drafted **Feb 26**, signed **Mar 10, 2026**, effective **Mar 15**: **34 seats**, term end **Mar 14, 2027**. Only seats and term-end changed; other earlier provisions remain. June’s March 11 email confirms countersignature/PDF and pending invoice request to Felix. [D040][D073]

### Operational history and prerequisites

- July 16 visit, recorded July 17 privately: Zanesville outbound Doors 8–12, Door 11 bent track locked out until Friday but selectable in product; **14:00** misroutes. Door 9/10 Zebra Wi-Fi drops when baler starts, roughly **six minutes/check-in** added walking for passes. Planned biweekly shipping checks, out-of-service instructions, print spooler/static-IP investigation, third-shift Dwell by Carrier report before July 25. [D087]
- March 2026 **4912**, Marietta Door 6 phantom lock after flatbed check-in; jockeys manually clear tablet slot; support review before second shift **14:00** requested. **SUP-4982**, March 17 open: Gate B Zebra mapping prints Dock 4 instead of Dock 12. [D073][D097]

## Marrow Fieldworks

Pree assigned January 2025; Tobias formal owner from **January 5, 2026**. Handoff included Salina Gate 3 barcode **4419**, Salina/Enid contacts, and open **4409** Gatehouse Check-In timeout at Salina North Bay 4/west grain-bin apron **06:00** flatbed intake plus **4412** overflow-lot combine SMS prompt glitch. [D054][D066][D011]

### Shared contract history

- MSA drafted **Mar 24**, signed **Apr 8**, effective **May 1, 2025–Apr 30, 2026**: Fieldworks **90 seats**, Agrisupply **25**, each **$1,800**, **10%**, Tier **2**. Separate entity rosters/subscriptions despite shared umbrella. [D029]

MAS quantity/SLA remain as affiliate amendment; no replacement discount is stated, earlier unmodified terms continue. Co-terminous end applies to both. [D042]
- April 23 CRM confirms Fieldworks **95/$1,880/Apr 30, 2027**, says MAS seats/SLA untouched. Chat clarifies ambiguous CRM header “Marrow” means parent; this task-label clarification does not erase renewal’s explicit affiliate pricing and term provisions. [D052][D020][D042]

Deployment/user rules: full entity names in requests, separate user rosters with business email/function, duplicate-name/email cleanup, no generic shift label in place of individual identity, marked test appointments not carrier instructions; receiving staff review site/door/shift/arrival instructions before live use. ### Launch and operational history

- February 2025 contracting while MAS called active. April signing call targets June launch starting Salina and two Kearney-area MAS cross-docks; Salina combine-header queue on County Road 14, Door 4 seed pallets; oversized tag/config discussed. Mapping CSV due Apr 11; billing hierarchy Apr 10; sandbox **ZD-44918** onboarding link. [D099][D075]
- June launch rehearsal late-truck move preserving arrival note; Door 4/D04 label normalization. June 20 says first **nine dealerships** went live week of **June 16**; duplicate Door 3 slots, missing driver texts, receiving report missing afternoon pickups remained. [D103][D077]

Tuesday delivery unchanged. [D081]

Trailer details wrongly in carrier field; long mobile notes hide unload instructions. Needed actual-length repro, two Door 3 examples, field-use one-page refresher and label tester, follow-up Nov 21. [D081]
- **SUP-4630**, Dec 2 investigating: west parts counter dealer SSO redirect loop, including private window; trace sent engineering, no workaround as of **09:37**. [D095]
- January handoff intro dates inconsistent within weekly: milestone Jan 7, prose Thursday morning check-in; Combine Bay B winter gates. [D111]
- April 22: Salina Gate 3 QR unreadable from glare; high-contrast/dark-mode inquiry, ticket uncertain “**PD-8841 maybe**.” Kearney Bay 4/5 departed trailers left open distorting Morning Yard Snapshot, narrator labels training issue; checkout PDF planned. [D083]

## Marrow Agrisupply

**MAS / Marrow Agri**, Plains farm supply retail chain under Marrow Fieldworks, moving baler twine, fencing, calf starter and other farm supplies. **Central pooled account since January 2025**, no single AM; Pree’s office hours or Hollis’s support work are not ownership assignments. ## Scope and provenance

This wiki compiles supplied records dated November 2024–September 2026, plus undated notes. Source references `[Dxxx]` identify provenance. Contract drafting, signature, and effective dates are kept distinct. Executed instruments, unsigned proposals, CRM claims, meeting recollections, and operational observations remain separately identified; later dates are not treated as automatic corrections.

Pemberline Systems supplies **Pemberline Dock**, yard and dock scheduling software. Contract descriptions include dispatcher consoles, gatehouse kiosks, carrier appointment portals, yard tracking/spotter tasking, and APIs. Those descriptions and commercial permissions are instrument-specific. [D024][D027][D028]

## Entity and alias directory

| Entity | Codes and aliases | Identification boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Brackenwater Freight Co. | **BWF**, **Bracken** | Great Lakes LTL carrier; Toledo HQ in account page. [D001][D024] |
| Quarrendon Freight Lines | **QFL**, **Q-Freight** | Customer; distinct from Quarendon Freightways. HQ/location descriptions differ across records. [D004][D028][D088] |
| Tamsin Cold Chain | **TCC** | Pacific Northwest refrigerated warehousing; not the textile mill. [D005][D019] |
| Thornbury Cloth Co. | **TCC**; formerly **Orrin Mills / ORM** | Same legal entity and tax ID after January 12, 2026 rename; not Tamsin. [D019][D039][D067] |
| Tansley Parcel | **TPCL** in board deck; **TPX** in old exports; ambiguous **TP** in chat | Regional parcel carrier; unrelated to Tansleigh Packaging. [D006][D007][D015] |
| Tansleigh Packaging | **TSP**; signed original order also says **TSP / TP** | Corrugated manufacturer. “Tansley Packaging” was explicitly corrected in chat. [D015][D027] |
| Marrow Fieldworks | **MFW**, sometimes “Marrow” | Parent equipment dealer network; separate account from its subsidiary. [D003][D020] |
| Marrow Agrisupply | **MAS**, **Marrow Agri** | Subsidiary/covered affiliate of MFW; Central pooled account. [D002][D029][D033] |
| Quarendon Freightways | Sometimes shortened “Quarendon” | Duluth-area trucking company using competitor yard software; not a Pemberline customer. Dispatcher Ellis formerly worked at QFL. [D088] |
| Stoneharrow Billing | Billing vendor | Pemberline is Felix Duarte’s vendor-side account, not a freight or retail customer account. [D071] |

Quarendon Freightways also appears as a carrier delivering to Tansleigh and Marrow locations. Marrow meeting notes describe its dispatchers using the standard guest carrier portal rather than customer logins. An inactive look-alike carrier-directory entry was to be hidden after erroneous selections sent confirmations to an unmonitored address. [D015][D075][D105]

| **Tobias Rendle** | Tansleigh owner as of May 19, 2025 private note; MFW owner since January 5, 2026. Ramp/start chronology has tension across sources. [D085][D099][D111] |
| **June Osei-Lark** | Deal desk and contracts manager; signature blocks, redlines, filing, billing handoffs; signs supplied provider-side contracts. [D014][D024–D044] |
| **Anselm Grieve** | CFO; approves discounts exceeding 10%; explicitly approved Tansley’s 14% and rejected QFL draft 15%. [D014][D031][D065] |

## ARTICLE 5. SUPPORT AND SERVICE LEVELS

**5.1 Support Tier Assignment.** During the active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall provide Customer with **Tier 2** Support Services for the Platform. Tier 2 Support Services are included in the annual subscription Fees set forth in Article 3 at no additional charge.

**5.2 Tier 2 Channels and Hours.** Under the Tier 2 support plan, Customer's designated system administrators (up to six (6) named individuals appointed by Customer's Director of Yard Operations) may submit support tickets via Pemberline's web-based support portal and by direct telephone hotline.
(a) **Severity 1 (Critical Yard Outage):** Telephone and portal support available twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year (24x7x365). A Severity 1 issue is defined as a complete inability of Authorized Users at one or more terminals to access the Platform, or a failure of core gate check-in or dock door assignment functions with no operational workaround, resulting in physical truck queues at terminal gates.
(b) **Severity 2 (Major Operational Degradation):** Support coverage available Monday through Saturday, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 2 issue is defined as a substantial impairment of primary features (such as yard jockey task dispatch latency, failure of EDI 214 status message transmission, or carrier portal booking failure) where core yard operations can continue via manual workaround within the Platform.
(c) **Severity 3 (Minor Feature Issue):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central Time, excluding US federal holidays. A Severity 3 issue is defined as a non-critical malfunction, reporting discrepancy, or user interface defect that has minimal impact on daily dock scheduling.
(d) **Severity 4 (Cosmetic or Inquiry):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 4 issue includes general "how-to" configuration questions, documentation requests, or cosmetic enhancement requests.

**5.3 Tier 2 Target Response Times.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline commits to the following initial human response times from the moment a ticket is logged in the support portal or received via the emergency telephone hotline:
* **Severity 1:** Within thirty (30) minutes, with continuous engineering engagement and status updates every sixty (60) minutes until service is restored.
* **Severity 2:** Within two (2) hours during covered hours, with status updates every four (4) hours.
* **Severity 3:** Within eight (8) business hours.
* **Severity 4:** Within two (2) business days.

**5.4 Platform Availability Commitment.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline shall maintain a Monthly Uptime Percentage for the production instance of the Platform of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%), measured across each calendar month. "Monthly Uptime Percentage" is calculated by subtracting from 100% the percentage of total minutes in the calendar month during which the Platform experienced Unscheduled Downtime.

**5.5 Exclusions from Unscheduled Downtime.** Unscheduled Downtime does not include unavailability resulting from: (a) Scheduled Maintenance windows occurring between Saturday 11:00 PM Central Time and Sunday 3:00 AM Central Time, provided Pemberline gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior electronic notice via the Platform status page; (b) Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 19.3; (c) failures of Customer's local yard Wi-Fi networks, cellular data terminals mounted in yard spotter cabs, barcode scanners, RFID gate readers, or local internet service providers; (d) interruptions caused by third-party transportation management systems (TMS) or warehouse management systems (WMS) integrated by Customer via API; or (e) suspension of Customer's access pursuant to Article 15.

**5.6 Service Credits.** If Pemberline fails to meet the 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage under the Tier 2 SLA in any given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit applied against its next invoice, calculated as a percentage of one-twelfth (1/12th) of the net annual subscription Fee ($18,993.33 USD monthly equivalent), as follows:
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 99.00% and 99.49%: Five percent (5%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 98.00% and 98.99%: Ten percent (10%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage below 98.00%: Twenty percent (20%) credit.
To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the Unscheduled Downtime occurred. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for any failure to meet the Tier 2 availability metrics, provided that if the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 97.00% for three (3) consecutive calendar months, Customer may treat such failure as a material breach under Section 16.2.

## ARTICLE 7. INFORMATION SECURITY AND PRIVACY

**7.1 Security Program.** Pemberline shall maintain a formal, written information security program that includes administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Customer Data against unauthorized access, destruction, modification, or disclosure. Such safeguards shall be no less rigorous than accepted industry standards for enterprise B2B software-as-a-service providers, including alignment with AICPA SOC 2 Type II Trust Services Criteria.

**7.2 Technical Controls.** Without limiting the generality of Section 7.1, Pemberline's technical safeguards shall include at a minimum: (a) encryption of all Customer Data in transit over public networks using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2 or higher); (b) encryption of all Customer Data at rest in database storage and backup volumes using Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit keys (AES-256); (c) logical tenant isolation in the application and database layers to prevent any other customer from accessing Customer Data; (d) support for Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML 2.0) single sign-on (SSO) integration and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all 140 Subscribed Seats; and (e) role-based access controls (RBAC) allowing Customer to restrict user permissions by terminal location and operational function.

**7.3 Audits and Certifications.** At least once every twelve (12) months, Pemberline shall engage an independent, certified third-party auditing firm to conduct a SOC 2 Type II examination of the controls governing the Platform. Upon Customer's written request (not more than once annually), Pemberline shall provide Customer with a confidential copy of its most recent SOC 2 Type II report and executive summary of its annual third-party penetration test, which shall be treated as Pemberline's Confidential Information under Article 8.

**7.4 Security Incident Notification.** In the event Pemberline confirms an unauthorized acquisition, access, alteration, or disclosure of unencrypted Customer Data residing on Pemberline's systems (a "Security Incident"), Pemberline shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of confirmation. Such notice shall be delivered to Customer's primary operational contact and legal department and shall describe the nature of the Security Incident, the categories of Customer Data affected, the root cause (to the extent then known), and the containment and remediation measures taken by Pemberline. Pemberline shall cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests for information necessary for Customer to comply with applicable data breach notification laws.

**7.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery.** Pemberline shall maintain and annually test a disaster recovery and business continuity plan for the Platform. The production environment for Pemberline Dock shall utilize redundant availability zones within the continental United States, configured to achieve a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of no more than fifteen (15) minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of no more than four (4) hours in the event of a catastrophic data center failure.

# Master Subscription Agreement: Marrow Fieldworks and Covered Affiliates

**Drafted:** 24 Mar 2025  
**Written and signed:** 8 Apr 2025  
**Effective date:** 1 May 2025

## 1. Parties and Purpose

1.1 This Master Subscription Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Marrow Fieldworks, for itself and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply (together, the “Customer”). Marrow Agrisupply is a subsidiary of Marrow Fieldworks and is expressly included within this Agreement.

1.2 This Agreement records the Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software. Marrow Fieldworks operates an agricultural equipment dealer network in the Plains. Marrow Agrisupply operates a farm supply retail chain in the Plains. Each entity’s subscription is separately identified below.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

2.1 This Agreement was drafted on 24 Mar 2025 and executed by the parties on 8 Apr 2025. The date of execution is distinct from the effective date.

2.2 The Agreement becomes effective on 1 May 2025. Preparatory activities before that date, including roster collection, site naming, and review of sample appointment records, do not alter the effective date or the subscription quantities stated herein.

2.3 The end of the current term, designated as the renewal date, is 30 Apr 2026 for both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply.

## 3. Subscription Schedule

3.1 The following subscription schedule applies:

| Subscribing entity | Subscribed seats | Price per seat per year (USD) | Discount | End of current term (renewal date) | Support SLA tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Marrow Fieldworks | 90 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | 25 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |

3.2 The stated annual per-seat price and discount apply to each entity listed in the schedule. The seat quantities are entity-specific: 90 seats apply to Marrow Fieldworks, and 25 seats apply to Marrow Agrisupply.

3.3 References to the Customer collectively shall not obscure the separate subscription entries. Administrative rosters, support submissions, and deployment worksheets shall identify the relevant subscribing entity by its full name.

## 4. Covered Affiliate

4.1 Marrow Agrisupply is the covered affiliate under this Agreement. Its inclusion permits its subscription to be administered within this master record while retaining the separate seat quantity shown in Section 3.

4.2 Marrow Fieldworks shall identify whether an operational request concerns Marrow Fieldworks, Marrow Agrisupply, or both. A request to configure a receiving calendar for Marrow Agrisupply shall not be treated as a request to change a Marrow Fieldworks calendar merely because the entities share an administrative contact.

4.3 Site labels shall distinguish the agricultural equipment receiving operation from the farm supply receiving operation. Similar location names shall be accompanied by the subscribing entity’s name in the deployment worksheet.

## 5. Deployment Records

5.1 The Customer shall prepare a deployment worksheet identifying site names, dock-door labels, receiving shifts, and personnel responsible for maintaining appointment calendars. The worksheet shall separate equipment deliveries from farm supply deliveries where those activities use different receiving areas.

5.2 Initial configuration review shall include representative appointment entries for an equipment unloading bay and a retail replenishment dock. Test entries shall be visibly marked as samples and shall not be issued to a carrier as live delivery instructions.

5.3 Where a location uses labels such as “Door 3” or “West Receiving,” the Customer shall use those labels consistently in its worksheet and appointment instructions. Informal directions such as “the usual gate” shall be replaced with the applicable site and receiving-area designation.

## 6. User Administration

6.1 The Customer shall maintain separate user rosters for Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply. Each roster shall identify the user’s business email address, subscribing entity, and operational function, including receiving clerk, dispatcher, or site administrator.

6.2 Shared shift responsibilities shall be described in the roster without substituting a generic shift label for an individual user’s identity. Departure and reassignment notices shall identify the affected user and entity so that administrative changes can be applied to the correct subscription record.

6.3 Before submitting a roster revision, the Customer shall check for duplicate entries caused by shortened names, alternate email addresses, or transfers between equipment and farm supply operations.

## 7. Appointment Information

7.1 The Customer shall supply operational information appropriate to yard and dock scheduling, including appointment reference, carrier name, scheduled arrival, destination site, and receiving location.

7.2 Appointment notes shall distinguish between scheduling instructions and descriptions of goods. For example, an instruction to report to the west gate shall be entered as an arrival instruction rather than embedded in a description of replacement tractor components.

7.3 The Customer shall review imported appointment data for obsolete door names, missing site references, and duplicate delivery references. A corrected import file shall identify the affected records rather than requiring receiving personnel to infer which appointment should remain active.

## 8. Support Administration

8.1 The support SLA tier applicable to both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply is Tier 2.

8.2 A support submission shall identify the subscribing entity, affected site, relevant appointment reference, observed behavior, and steps preceding the issue. Where available, the submission shall include a screenshot showing the affected calendar or appointment view.

8.3 For a report that an appointment appears under the wrong receiving shift, the Customer shall include the intended shift and the displayed shift. For a report concerning a missing dock-door label, the Customer shall provide the label used in its deployment worksheet. These particulars support investigation and do not change the subscribed support tier.

## 9. Operational Review

9.1 The Customer’s receiving personnel shall review sample calendars before using them for live scheduling. Review shall cover site selection, door naming, shift boundaries, and the clarity of carrier-facing arrival instructions.

9.2 Review comments shall identify a specific screen, field, or appointment example. A comment such as “wrong dock” shall be supplemented with the intended receiving location.

9.3 The parties shall maintain deployment corrections separately from the subscription schedule. Correcting a door label or removing a duplicate sample appointment shall not amend the commercial entries in Section 3.

## 10. Executed Record

10.1 The signature block below records execution on 8 Apr 2025. The effective date remains 1 May 2025.

10.2 The customer signatory executes this Agreement for Marrow Fieldworks and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply.

I promised I would get you the root-cause write-up from our platform folks as soon as they finished their post-mortem coffee, so here is the full scoop on what happened on 3 Sep 2025.

Basically, at 06:14 CDT yesterday, a routine worker node patch in our US-Central cluster introduced a bad retry loop on the carrier webhook listener inside Pemberline Dock. Whenever an inbound manifest ping timed out—which happens plenty during the 6am shift change—instead of backing off, the service fired immediate duplicate retries. That flooded the queue and locked up the live gate check-in screen for Tansley Parcel until engineering rolled the patch back at 07:48 CDT (ticket #INC-8841).

Nobody wants to be out in that humidity squinting at paper BOLs. To make sure this doesn't bite us again, engineering has already capped retry concurrency and split the webhook queue off from the main dock board service.

Because we obviously dropped the ball during your peak window, Hollis and I spoke with June Osei-Lark on our side this morning, and we want to put a goodwill service credit on your next invoice. Just reply with a quick thumbs-up if you are good with us applying that credit, and I will have June get it squared away with Stoneharrow Billing today.

Let me know if your ops director wants to hop on a fifteen-minute call to grill our engineers on the fix—happy to set that up!

Best,
Pree

WHEREAS, the Parties desire to establish the terms and conditions under which Pemberline will grant Customer access to the Platform and provide associated support services, as further specified in the Order Schedule attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, representations, warranties, and undertakings set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

---

## ARTICLE 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 "Affiliate"** means, with respect to any entity, any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such entity, where "control" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or equity interests of such entity, or the power to direct the management and policies of such entity.

**1.2 "Authorized User"** means an individual employee, yard clerk, gate guard, dispatcher, terminal manager, or dedicated third-party contractor of Customer who has been assigned a unique username and credential set by Customer to access and use the Platform under a Subscribed Seat.

**1.3 "Confidential Information"** has the meaning set forth in Section 8.1 of this Agreement.

**1.4 "Customer Data"** means all electronic data, text, records, carrier bills of lading numbers, tractor and trailer identifiers, seal numbers, driver check-in logs, dock door schedules, yard spot maps, Detention and Demurrage timestamps, and other operational information submitted, uploaded, imported, or transmitted by or on behalf of Customer or its Authorized Users into the Platform.

**1.5 "Documentation"** means the user manuals, release notes, administrator guides, API specifications, and online help files published by Pemberline from time to time and made generally available to subscribers of Pemberline Dock.

**1.6 "Effective Date"** means 4/1/25, which is the date on which the subscription rights, operational access, and service level obligations under this Agreement commence, distinct from the Execution Date of 3/28/25 on which the Parties signed this Agreement.

**1.7 "Order Schedule"** means the initial ordering document attached hereto as Schedule A, and any subsequent written ordering document executed by both Parties that references this Agreement.

**1.8 "Platform"** means the hosted, multi-tenant software-as-a-service application known as Pemberline Dock, including its web-based dispatcher console, gatehouse kiosk view, carrier self-scheduling portal, yard spotter task module, and standard application programming interfaces (APIs), as updated or modified by Pemberline from time to time in accordance with this Agreement.

**1.9 "Subscribed Seat"** means a single named-user license provisioned within the Platform for one (1) Authorized User. **1.10 "Support Services"** means the technical support, maintenance, bug fixing, and operational assistance provided by Pemberline in accordance with the Tier 2 service level commitments described in Article 5.

## ARTICLE 2. SUBSCRIPTION GRANT AND SEATS

**2.1 Provision of Access.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and Customer's timely payment of all applicable Fees, Pemberline hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable (except as permitted under Article 17), non-sublicensable, worldwide right during the active period of this Agreement to access and use the Platform and Documentation solely for Customer's internal business operations in managing its freight terminals, yards, and loading docks.

**2.2 Subscribed Seats.** As of the Effective Date (4/1/25), Customer subscribes to exactly one hundred forty (140) Subscribed Seats of Pemberline Dock. Customer may allocate these 140 Subscribed Seats across its operational terminals, including its Saint Paul hub, Duluth yard, Eau Claire cross-dock, and Des Moines relay station, at the discretion of Customer's system administrators.

**2.3 Seat Assignment and Reassignment.** Each of the 140 Subscribed Seats must be tied to a unique individual identity (using corporate email address or employee badge ID) within the Platform's identity management directory. Customer may not configure generic, shared, or role-based credentials (such as "gatehouse1@qfl.example" or "nightdispatch@qfl.example") to allow multiple individuals on rotating shifts to utilize a single Subscribed Seat. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may permanently reassign a Subscribed Seat from one individual to another without penalty when an Authorized User terminates employment, transfers out of yard or dock operations, or goes on extended leave exceeding fourteen (14) consecutive calendar days.

**2.4 Seat Audits and True-Up.** Pemberline's Platform includes automated seat-count enforcement that prevents the provisioning of active credentials beyond the 140 Subscribed Seats unless an administrator with purchasing authority initiates an expansion request. If Customer requires additional seats during an active period, Customer may order additional Subscribed Seats in minimum blocks of five (5) seats by executing an addendum to the Order Schedule. Any mid-period seat additions shall be priced at the discounted net rate set forth in Section 3.1, prorated for the remainder of the then-current period.

**2.5 Reservation of Rights.** This Agreement is a subscription agreement for access to hosted software services and is not a sale of software or intellectual property. Customer acknowledges that it is obtaining only a limited right to access and use the Platform as hosted by Pemberline, and that irrespective of any use of the words "purchase," "sale," or "seat" hereunder, no ownership rights are being conveyed to Customer under this Agreement.

The standard list price for Pemberline Dock is one thousand eight hundred fifty United States Dollars ($1,850.00 USD) per Subscribed Seat per year. Under this Agreement, Pemberline grants Customer a contractual discount of twelve percent (12%) off the standard list price, resulting in a net discounted price of one thousand six hundred twenty-eight United States Dollars ($1,628.00 USD) per Subscribed Seat per year.

**3.2 Total Annual Commitment.** Based on the subscription of 140 Subscribed Seats at the list price of $1,850.00 USD per seat per year ($259,000.00 USD gross annual value), less the twelve percent (12%) discount ($31,080.00 USD annual discount), Customer's total net annual subscription Fee for the initial twelve-month period beginning on 4/1/25 and ending on 3/31/26 is two hundred twenty-seven thousand nine hundred twenty United States Dollars ($227,920.00 USD).

**3.3 Non-Cancelable and Non-Refundable.** Except as expressly provided in Section 11.3 (Warranty Remedies), Section 12.1 (Intellectual Property Infringement Mitigation), or Section 16.2 (Termination for Cause by Customer), all Fees are non-cancelable and non-refundable once invoiced. **3.4 Taxes.** All Fees stated herein are exclusive of any federal, state, local, municipal, or foreign sales, use, value-added, excise, gross receipts, or other taxes, duties, or governmental assessments ("Taxes"). **4.3 Disputed Invoices.** If Customer in good faith disputes any portion of an invoice, Customer must notify Pemberline's finance department in writing within twenty (20) calendar days of the invoice date, specifying the invoice number, the exact dollar amount in dispute, and a reasonably detailed explanation with supporting documentation for the basis of the dispute. **4.4 Late Payments.** Any undisputed amount not received by Pemberline within the Net 45 payment period shall accrue late interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower, calculated from the forty-sixth (46th) day following the invoice date until the date paid in full. In addition to late interest, if an undisputed invoice remains unpaid more than fifteen (15) calendar days past its Net 45 due date, Pemberline shall have the right to exercise its suspension remedies under Article 15.

**4.5 Purchase Orders.** If Customer requires a purchase order number to be referenced on invoices for its internal accounting procedures, Customer shall provide such purchase order number upon execution of this Agreement on 3/28/25. ## ARTICLE 5. SUPPORT AND SERVICE LEVELS

**5.1 Support Tier Assignment.** During the active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall provide Customer with **Tier 2** Support Services for the Platform. Tier 2 Support Services are included in the annual subscription Fees set forth in Article 3 at no additional charge.

**5.2 Tier 2 Channels and Hours.** Under the Tier 2 support plan, Customer's designated system administrators (up to six (6) named individuals appointed by Customer's Director of Yard Operations) may submit support tickets via Pemberline's web-based support portal and by direct telephone hotline.
(a) **Severity 1 (Critical Yard Outage):** Telephone and portal support available twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year (24x7x365). A Severity 1 issue is defined as a complete inability of Authorized Users at one or more terminals to access the Platform, or a failure of core gate check-in or dock door assignment functions with no operational workaround, resulting in physical truck queues at terminal gates.
(b) **Severity 2 (Major Operational Degradation):** Support coverage available Monday through Saturday, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 2 issue is defined as a substantial impairment of primary features (such as yard jockey task dispatch latency, failure of EDI 214 status message transmission, or carrier portal booking failure) where core yard operations can continue via manual workaround within the Platform.
(c) **Severity 3 (Minor Feature Issue):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central Time, excluding US federal holidays. A Severity 3 issue is defined as a non-critical malfunction, reporting discrepancy, or user interface defect that has minimal impact on daily dock scheduling.
(d) **Severity 4 (Cosmetic or Inquiry):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 4 issue includes general "how-to" configuration questions, documentation requests, or cosmetic enhancement requests.

**5.3 Tier 2 Target Response Times.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline commits to the following initial human response times from the moment a ticket is logged in the support portal or received via the emergency telephone hotline:
* **Severity 1:** Within thirty (30) minutes, with continuous engineering engagement and status updates every sixty (60) minutes until service is restored.
* **Severity 2:** Within two (2) hours during covered hours, with status updates every four (4) hours.
* **Severity 3:** Within eight (8) business hours.
* **Severity 4:** Within two (2) business days.

**5.4 Platform Availability Commitment.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline shall maintain a Monthly Uptime Percentage for the production instance of the Platform of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%), measured across each calendar month. **5.5 Exclusions from Unscheduled Downtime.** Unscheduled Downtime does not include unavailability resulting from: (a) Scheduled Maintenance windows occurring between Saturday 11:00 PM Central Time and Sunday 3:00 AM Central Time, provided Pemberline gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior electronic notice via the Platform status page; (b) Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 19.3; (c) failures of Customer's local yard Wi-Fi networks, cellular data terminals mounted in yard spotter cabs, barcode scanners, RFID gate readers, or local internet service providers; (d) interruptions caused by third-party transportation management systems (TMS) or warehouse management systems (WMS) integrated by Customer via API; or (e) suspension of Customer's access pursuant to Article 15.

**5.6 Service Credits.** If Pemberline fails to meet the 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage under the Tier 2 SLA in any given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit applied against its next invoice, calculated as a percentage of one-twelfth (1/12th) of the net annual subscription Fee ($18,993.33 USD monthly equivalent), as follows:
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 99.00% and 99.49%: Five percent (5%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 98.00% and 98.99%: Ten percent (10%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage below 98.00%: Twenty percent (20%) credit.
To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the Unscheduled Downtime occurred. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for any failure to meet the Tier 2 availability metrics, provided that if the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 97.00% for three (3) consecutive calendar months, Customer may treat such failure as a material breach under Section 16.2.

# Master Subscription Agreement: Marrow Fieldworks and Covered Affiliates

**Drafted:** 24 Mar 2025  
**Written and signed:** 8 Apr 2025  
**Effective date:** 1 May 2025

## 1. Parties and Purpose

1.1 This Master Subscription Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Marrow Fieldworks, for itself and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply (together, the “Customer”). Marrow Agrisupply is a subsidiary of Marrow Fieldworks and is expressly included within this Agreement.

1.2 This Agreement records the Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software. Marrow Fieldworks operates an agricultural equipment dealer network in the Plains. Marrow Agrisupply operates a farm supply retail chain in the Plains. Each entity’s subscription is separately identified below.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

2.1 This Agreement was drafted on 24 Mar 2025 and executed by the parties on 8 Apr 2025. The date of execution is distinct from the effective date.

2.2 The Agreement becomes effective on 1 May 2025. Preparatory activities before that date, including roster collection, site naming, and review of sample appointment records, do not alter the effective date or the subscription quantities stated herein.

2.3 The end of the current term, designated as the renewal date, is 30 Apr 2026 for both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply.

## 3. Subscription Schedule

3.1 The following subscription schedule applies:

| Subscribing entity | Subscribed seats | Price per seat per year (USD) | Discount | End of current term (renewal date) | Support SLA tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Marrow Fieldworks | 90 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | 25 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |

3.2 The stated annual per-seat price and discount apply to each entity listed in the schedule. The seat quantities are entity-specific: 90 seats apply to Marrow Fieldworks, and 25 seats apply to Marrow Agrisupply.

3.3 References to the Customer collectively shall not obscure the separate subscription entries. Administrative rosters, support submissions, and deployment worksheets shall identify the relevant subscribing entity by its full name.

## 4. Covered Affiliate

4.1 Marrow Agrisupply is the covered affiliate under this Agreement. Its inclusion permits its subscription to be administered within this master record while retaining the separate seat quantity shown in Section 3.

4.2 Marrow Fieldworks shall identify whether an operational request concerns Marrow Fieldworks, Marrow Agrisupply, or both. A request to configure a receiving calendar for Marrow Agrisupply shall not be treated as a request to change a Marrow Fieldworks calendar merely because the entities share an administrative contact.

4.3 Site labels shall distinguish the agricultural equipment receiving operation from the farm supply receiving operation. Similar location names shall be accompanied by the subscribing entity’s name in the deployment worksheet.

## 5. Deployment Records

5.1 The Customer shall prepare a deployment worksheet identifying site names, dock-door labels, receiving shifts, and personnel responsible for maintaining appointment calendars. The worksheet shall separate equipment deliveries from farm supply deliveries where those activities use different receiving areas.

5.2 Initial configuration review shall include representative appointment entries for an equipment unloading bay and a retail replenishment dock. Test entries shall be visibly marked as samples and shall not be issued to a carrier as live delivery instructions.

5.3 Where a location uses labels such as “Door 3” or “West Receiving,” the Customer shall use those labels consistently in its worksheet and appointment instructions. Informal directions such as “the usual gate” shall be replaced with the applicable site and receiving-area designation.

## 6. User Administration

6.1 The Customer shall maintain separate user rosters for Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply. Each roster shall identify the user’s business email address, subscribing entity, and operational function, including receiving clerk, dispatcher, or site administrator.

**From:** Priyanka "Pree" Sundaram <psundaram@pemberline.com>

**Cc:** Hollis Mbeki <hmbeki@pemberline.com>

Hi Lev,

Hope you are surviving the Thursday morning rush! And more importantly, hope the Tulsa yard is back to breathing normally today after yesterday's chaos. I promised I would get you the root-cause write-up from our platform folks as soon as they finished their post-mortem coffee, so here is the full scoop on what happened on 3 Sep 2025.

Basically, at 06:14 CDT yesterday, a routine worker node patch in our US-Central cluster introduced a bad retry loop on the carrier webhook listener inside Pemberline Dock. Whenever an inbound manifest ping timed out—which happens plenty during the 6am shift change—instead of backing off, the service fired immediate duplicate retries. That flooded the queue and locked up the live gate check-in screen for Tansley Parcel until engineering rolled the patch back at 07:48 CDT (ticket #INC-8841). 

I know that ninety-four minutes right at morning dispatch meant your guards at Doors 12 through 18 had to go back to clipboards and radio checks while five linehaul rigs backed up onto the service road. Nobody wants to be out in that humidity squinting at paper BOLs. To make sure this doesn't bite us again, engineering has already capped retry concurrency and split the webhook queue off from the main dock board service.

Because we obviously dropped the ball during your peak window, Hollis and I spoke with June Osei-Lark on our side this morning, and we want to put a goodwill service credit on your next invoice. Just reply with a quick thumbs-up if you are good with us applying that credit, and I will have June get it squared away with Stoneharrow Billing today.

Let me know if your ops director wants to hop on a fifteen-minute call to grill our engineers on the fix—happy to set that up!

Best,
Pree

## ARTICLE 5. SUPPORT AND SERVICE LEVELS

**5.1 Support Tier Assignment.** During the active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall provide Customer with **Tier 2** Support Services for the Platform. Tier 2 Support Services are included in the annual subscription Fees set forth in Article 3 at no additional charge.

**5.2 Tier 2 Channels and Hours.** Under the Tier 2 support plan, Customer's designated system administrators (up to six (6) named individuals appointed by Customer's Director of Yard Operations) may submit support tickets via Pemberline's web-based support portal and by direct telephone hotline.
(a) **Severity 1 (Critical Yard Outage):** Telephone and portal support available twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year (24x7x365). A Severity 1 issue is defined as a complete inability of Authorized Users at one or more terminals to access the Platform, or a failure of core gate check-in or dock door assignment functions with no operational workaround, resulting in physical truck queues at terminal gates.
(b) **Severity 2 (Major Operational Degradation):** Support coverage available Monday through Saturday, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 2 issue is defined as a substantial impairment of primary features (such as yard jockey task dispatch latency, failure of EDI 214 status message transmission, or carrier portal booking failure) where core yard operations can continue via manual workaround within the Platform.
(c) **Severity 3 (Minor Feature Issue):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central Time, excluding US federal holidays. A Severity 3 issue is defined as a non-critical malfunction, reporting discrepancy, or user interface defect that has minimal impact on daily dock scheduling.
(d) **Severity 4 (Cosmetic or Inquiry):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 4 issue includes general "how-to" configuration questions, documentation requests, or cosmetic enhancement requests.

**5.3 Tier 2 Target Response Times.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline commits to the following initial human response times from the moment a ticket is logged in the support portal or received via the emergency telephone hotline:
* **Severity 1:** Within thirty (30) minutes, with continuous engineering engagement and status updates every sixty (60) minutes until service is restored.
* **Severity 2:** Within two (2) hours during covered hours, with status updates every four (4) hours.
* **Severity 3:** Within eight (8) business hours.
* **Severity 4:** Within two (2) business days.

**5.4 Platform Availability Commitment.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline shall maintain a Monthly Uptime Percentage for the production instance of the Platform of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%), measured across each calendar month. "Monthly Uptime Percentage" is calculated by subtracting from 100% the percentage of total minutes in the calendar month during which the Platform experienced Unscheduled Downtime.

**5.5 Exclusions from Unscheduled Downtime.** Unscheduled Downtime does not include unavailability resulting from: (a) Scheduled Maintenance windows occurring between Saturday 11:00 PM Central Time and Sunday 3:00 AM Central Time, provided Pemberline gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior electronic notice via the Platform status page; (b) Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 19.3; (c) failures of Customer's local yard Wi-Fi networks, cellular data terminals mounted in yard spotter cabs, barcode scanners, RFID gate readers, or local internet service providers; (d) interruptions caused by third-party transportation management systems (TMS) or warehouse management systems (WMS) integrated by Customer via API; or (e) suspension of Customer's access pursuant to Article 15.

**5.6 Service Credits.** If Pemberline fails to meet the 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage under the Tier 2 SLA in any given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit applied against its next invoice, calculated as a percentage of one-twelfth (1/12th) of the net annual subscription Fee ($18,993.33 USD monthly equivalent), as follows:
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 99.00% and 99.49%: Five percent (5%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 98.00% and 98.99%: Ten percent (10%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage below 98.00%: Twenty percent (20%) credit.
To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the Unscheduled Downtime occurred. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for any failure to meet the Tier 2 availability metrics, provided that if the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 97.00% for three (3) consecutive calendar months, Customer may treat such failure as a material breach under Section 16.2.

## ARTICLE 7. INFORMATION SECURITY AND PRIVACY

**7.1 Security Program.** Pemberline shall maintain a formal, written information security program that includes administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Customer Data against unauthorized access, destruction, modification, or disclosure. Such safeguards shall be no less rigorous than accepted industry standards for enterprise B2B software-as-a-service providers, including alignment with AICPA SOC 2 Type II Trust Services Criteria.

**7.2 Technical Controls.** Without limiting the generality of Section 7.1, Pemberline's technical safeguards shall include at a minimum: (a) encryption of all Customer Data in transit over public networks using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2 or higher); (b) encryption of all Customer Data at rest in database storage and backup volumes using Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit keys (AES-256); (c) logical tenant isolation in the application and database layers to prevent any other customer from accessing Customer Data; (d) support for Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML 2.0) single sign-on (SSO) integration and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all 140 Subscribed Seats; and (e) role-based access controls (RBAC) allowing Customer to restrict user permissions by terminal location and operational function.

**7.3 Audits and Certifications.** At least once every twelve (12) months, Pemberline shall engage an independent, certified third-party auditing firm to conduct a SOC 2 Type II examination of the controls governing the Platform. Upon Customer's written request (not more than once annually), Pemberline shall provide Customer with a confidential copy of its most recent SOC 2 Type II report and executive summary of its annual third-party penetration test, which shall be treated as Pemberline's Confidential Information under Article 8.

**7.4 Security Incident Notification.** In the event Pemberline confirms an unauthorized acquisition, access, alteration, or disclosure of unencrypted Customer Data residing on Pemberline's systems (a "Security Incident"), Pemberline shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of confirmation. Such notice shall be delivered to Customer's primary operational contact and legal department and shall describe the nature of the Security Incident, the categories of Customer Data affected, the root cause (to the extent then known), and the containment and remediation measures taken by Pemberline. Pemberline shall cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests for information necessary for Customer to comply with applicable data breach notification laws.

**7.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery.** Pemberline shall maintain and annually test a disaster recovery and business continuity plan for the Platform. The production environment for Pemberline Dock shall utilize redundant availability zones within the continental United States, configured to achieve a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of no more than fifteen (15) minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of no more than four (4) hours in the event of a catastrophic data center failure.

# Master Subscription Agreement: Marrow Fieldworks and Covered Affiliates

**Drafted:** 24 Mar 2025  
**Written and signed:** 8 Apr 2025  
**Effective date:** 1 May 2025

## 1. Parties and Purpose

1.1 This Master Subscription Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Marrow Fieldworks, for itself and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply (together, the “Customer”). Marrow Agrisupply is a subsidiary of Marrow Fieldworks and is expressly included within this Agreement.

1.2 This Agreement records the Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software. Marrow Fieldworks operates an agricultural equipment dealer network in the Plains. Marrow Agrisupply operates a farm supply retail chain in the Plains. Each entity’s subscription is separately identified below.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

2.1 This Agreement was drafted on 24 Mar 2025 and executed by the parties on 8 Apr 2025. The date of execution is distinct from the effective date.

2.2 The Agreement becomes effective on 1 May 2025. Preparatory activities before that date, including roster collection, site naming, and review of sample appointment records, do not alter the effective date or the subscription quantities stated herein.

2.3 The end of the current term, designated as the renewal date, is 30 Apr 2026 for both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply.

## 3. Subscription Schedule

3.1 The following subscription schedule applies:

| Subscribing entity | Subscribed seats | Price per seat per year (USD) | Discount | End of current term (renewal date) | Support SLA tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Marrow Fieldworks | 90 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | 25 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |

3.2 The stated annual per-seat price and discount apply to each entity listed in the schedule. The seat quantities are entity-specific: 90 seats apply to Marrow Fieldworks, and 25 seats apply to Marrow Agrisupply.

3.3 References to the Customer collectively shall not obscure the separate subscription entries. Administrative rosters, support submissions, and deployment worksheets shall identify the relevant subscribing entity by its full name.

## 4. Covered Affiliate

4.1 Marrow Agrisupply is the covered affiliate under this Agreement. Its inclusion permits its subscription to be administered within this master record while retaining the separate seat quantity shown in Section 3.

4.2 Marrow Fieldworks shall identify whether an operational request concerns Marrow Fieldworks, Marrow Agrisupply, or both. A request to configure a receiving calendar for Marrow Agrisupply shall not be treated as a request to change a Marrow Fieldworks calendar merely because the entities share an administrative contact.

4.3 Site labels shall distinguish the agricultural equipment receiving operation from the farm supply receiving operation. Similar location names shall be accompanied by the subscribing entity’s name in the deployment worksheet.

## 5. Deployment Records

5.1 The Customer shall prepare a deployment worksheet identifying site names, dock-door labels, receiving shifts, and personnel responsible for maintaining appointment calendars. The worksheet shall separate equipment deliveries from farm supply deliveries where those activities use different receiving areas.

5.2 Initial configuration review shall include representative appointment entries for an equipment unloading bay and a retail replenishment dock. Test entries shall be visibly marked as samples and shall not be issued to a carrier as live delivery instructions.

5.3 Where a location uses labels such as “Door 3” or “West Receiving,” the Customer shall use those labels consistently in its worksheet and appointment instructions. Informal directions such as “the usual gate” shall be replaced with the applicable site and receiving-area designation.

## 6. User Administration

6.1 The Customer shall maintain separate user rosters for Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply. Each roster shall identify the user’s business email address, subscribing entity, and operational function, including receiving clerk, dispatcher, or site administrator.

6.2 Shared shift responsibilities shall be described in the roster without substituting a generic shift label for an individual user’s identity. Departure and reassignment notices shall identify the affected user and entity so that administrative changes can be applied to the correct subscription record.

6.3 Before submitting a roster revision, the Customer shall check for duplicate entries caused by shortened names, alternate email addresses, or transfers between equipment and farm supply operations.

## 7. Appointment Information

7.1 The Customer shall supply operational information appropriate to yard and dock scheduling, including appointment reference, carrier name, scheduled arrival, destination site, and receiving location.

7.2 Appointment notes shall distinguish between scheduling instructions and descriptions of goods. For example, an instruction to report to the west gate shall be entered as an arrival instruction rather than embedded in a description of replacement tractor components.

7.3 The Customer shall review imported appointment data for obsolete door names, missing site references, and duplicate delivery references. A corrected import file shall identify the affected records rather than requiring receiving personnel to infer which appointment should remain active.

## 8. Support Administration

8.1 The support SLA tier applicable to both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply is Tier 2.

8.2 A support submission shall identify the subscribing entity, affected site, relevant appointment reference, observed behavior, and steps preceding the issue. Where available, the submission shall include a screenshot showing the affected calendar or appointment view.

8.3 For a report that an appointment appears under the wrong receiving shift, the Customer shall include the intended shift and the displayed shift. For a report concerning a missing dock-door label, the Customer shall provide the label used in its deployment worksheet. These particulars support investigation and do not change the subscribed support tier.

## 9. Operational Review

9.1 The Customer’s receiving personnel shall review sample calendars before using them for live scheduling. Review shall cover site selection, door naming, shift boundaries, and the clarity of carrier-facing arrival instructions.

9.2 Review comments shall identify a specific screen, field, or appointment example. A comment such as “wrong dock” shall be supplemented with the intended receiving location.

9.3 The parties shall maintain deployment corrections separately from the subscription schedule. Correcting a door label or removing a duplicate sample appointment shall not amend the commercial entries in Section 3.

# Master Subscription Agreement: Marrow Fieldworks and Covered Affiliates

**Drafted:** 24 Mar 2025  
**Written and signed:** 8 Apr 2025  
**Effective date:** 1 May 2025

## 1. Parties and Purpose

1.1 This Master Subscription Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Marrow Fieldworks, for itself and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply (together, the “Customer”). Marrow Agrisupply is a subsidiary of Marrow Fieldworks and is expressly included within this Agreement.

1.2 This Agreement records the Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software. Marrow Fieldworks operates an agricultural equipment dealer network in the Plains. Marrow Agrisupply operates a farm supply retail chain in the Plains. Each entity’s subscription is separately identified below.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

2.1 This Agreement was drafted on 24 Mar 2025 and executed by the parties on 8 Apr 2025. The date of execution is distinct from the effective date.

2.2 The Agreement becomes effective on 1 May 2025. Preparatory activities before that date, including roster collection, site naming, and review of sample appointment records, do not alter the effective date or the subscription quantities stated herein.

2.3 The end of the current term, designated as the renewal date, is 30 Apr 2026 for both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply.

## 3. Subscription Schedule

3.1 The following subscription schedule applies:

| Subscribing entity | Subscribed seats | Price per seat per year (USD) | Discount | End of current term (renewal date) | Support SLA tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Marrow Fieldworks | 90 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | 25 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |

3.2 The stated annual per-seat price and discount apply to each entity listed in the schedule. The seat quantities are entity-specific: 90 seats apply to Marrow Fieldworks, and 25 seats apply to Marrow Agrisupply.

3.3 References to the Customer collectively shall not obscure the separate subscription entries. Administrative rosters, support submissions, and deployment worksheets shall identify the relevant subscribing entity by its full name.

## 4. Covered Affiliate

4.1 Marrow Agrisupply is the covered affiliate under this Agreement. Its inclusion permits its subscription to be administered within this master record while retaining the separate seat quantity shown in Section 3.

4.2 Marrow Fieldworks shall identify whether an operational request concerns Marrow Fieldworks, Marrow Agrisupply, or both. A request to configure a receiving calendar for Marrow Agrisupply shall not be treated as a request to change a Marrow Fieldworks calendar merely because the entities share an administrative contact.

4.3 Site labels shall distinguish the agricultural equipment receiving operation from the farm supply receiving operation. Similar location names shall be accompanied by the subscribing entity’s name in the deployment worksheet.

## 5. Deployment Records

5.1 The Customer shall prepare a deployment worksheet identifying site names, dock-door labels, receiving shifts, and personnel responsible for maintaining appointment calendars. The worksheet shall separate equipment deliveries from farm supply deliveries where those activities use different receiving areas.

5.2 Initial configuration review shall include representative appointment entries for an equipment unloading bay and a retail replenishment dock. Test entries shall be visibly marked as samples and shall not be issued to a carrier as live delivery instructions.

5.3 Where a location uses labels such as “Door 3” or “West Receiving,” the Customer shall use those labels consistently in its worksheet and appointment instructions. Informal directions such as “the usual gate” shall be replaced with the applicable site and receiving-area designation.

## 6. User Administration

6.1 The Customer shall maintain separate user rosters for Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply. Each roster shall identify the user’s business email address, subscribing entity, and operational function, including receiving clerk, dispatcher, or site administrator.

6.2 Shared shift responsibilities shall be described in the roster without substituting a generic shift label for an individual user’s identity. Departure and reassignment notices shall identify the affected user and entity so that administrative changes can be applied to the correct subscription record.

6.3 Before submitting a roster revision, the Customer shall check for duplicate entries caused by shortened names, alternate email addresses, or transfers between equipment and farm supply operations.

## 7. Appointment Information

7.1 The Customer shall supply operational information appropriate to yard and dock scheduling, including appointment reference, carrier name, scheduled arrival, destination site, and receiving location.

7.2 Appointment notes shall distinguish between scheduling instructions and descriptions of goods. For example, an instruction to report to the west gate shall be entered as an arrival instruction rather than embedded in a description of replacement tractor components.

7.3 The Customer shall review imported appointment data for obsolete door names, missing site references, and duplicate delivery references. A corrected import file shall identify the affected records rather than requiring receiving personnel to infer which appointment should remain active.

## 8. Support Administration

8.1 The support SLA tier applicable to both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply is Tier 2.

8.2 A support submission shall identify the subscribing entity, affected site, relevant appointment reference, observed behavior, and steps preceding the issue. Where available, the submission shall include a screenshot showing the affected calendar or appointment view.

8.3 For a report that an appointment appears under the wrong receiving shift, the Customer shall include the intended shift and the displayed shift. For a report concerning a missing dock-door label, the Customer shall provide the label used in its deployment worksheet. These particulars support investigation and do not change the subscribed support tier.

## 9. Operational Review

9.1 The Customer’s receiving personnel shall review sample calendars before using them for live scheduling. Review shall cover site selection, door naming, shift boundaries, and the clarity of carrier-facing arrival instructions.

9.2 Review comments shall identify a specific screen, field, or appointment example. A comment such as “wrong dock” shall be supplemented with the intended receiving location.

9.3 The parties shall maintain deployment corrections separately from the subscription schedule. Correcting a door label or removing a duplicate sample appointment shall not amend the commercial entries in Section 3.

## 10. Executed Record

10.1 The signature block below records execution on 8 Apr 2025. The effective date remains 1 May 2025.

10.2 The customer signatory executes this Agreement for Marrow Fieldworks and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply.

I promised I would get you the root-cause write-up from our platform folks as soon as they finished their post-mortem coffee, so here is the full scoop on what happened on 3 Sep 2025.

Basically, at 06:14 CDT yesterday, a routine worker node patch in our US-Central cluster introduced a bad retry loop on the carrier webhook listener inside Pemberline Dock. Whenever an inbound manifest ping timed out—which happens plenty during the 6am shift change—instead of backing off, the service fired immediate duplicate retries. That flooded the queue and locked up the live gate check-in screen for Tansley Parcel until engineering rolled the patch back at 07:48 CDT (ticket #INC-8841). 

I know that ninety-four minutes right at morning dispatch meant your guards at Doors 12 through 18 had to go back to clipboards and radio checks while five linehaul rigs backed up onto the service road. Nobody wants to be out in that humidity squinting at paper BOLs. To make sure this doesn't bite us again, engineering has already capped retry concurrency and split the webhook queue off from the main dock board service.

Because we obviously dropped the ball during your peak window, Hollis and I spoke with June Osei-Lark on our side this morning, and we want to put a goodwill service credit on your next invoice. Just reply with a quick thumbs-up if you are good with us applying that credit, and I will have June get it squared away with Stoneharrow Billing today.

Let me know if your ops director wants to hop on a fifteen-minute call to grill our engineers on the fix—happy to set that up!

Pree

## Evidence, scope, and interpretation

This wiki compiles supplied records dated November 2024–September 2026, plus undated notes. Source IDs identify provenance; a reported status remains a source-specific status unless another record documents its resolution. Requests, draft terms, workarounds, planned deployments, and reported usage are not automatically executed commitments or evidence of approved strategy.

### Source authority and limitations

- Executed contracts establish the stated terms for their defined periods and expressly limited amendments. Drafting, execution, record-entry, effective, and term-end dates are distinct. Operational preparation and roster changes do not advance contractual effectiveness. [D024–D044]
- Emails, CRM entries, meeting notes, weekly updates, chats, and assistant digests preserve operational context but sometimes conflict with signed documents or one another. These conflicts remain visible below rather than being reconciled by source recency.
- Some documents lack a `status: signed` metadata field but contain completed execution blocks: Tansley Amendment 1, QFL Amendment 1, Brackenwater’s 2025 renewal, and Tansleigh’s 2026 renewal. Their bodies document execution. [D031][D032][D035][D040]
- Explicitly nonexecuted records are Brackenwater’s October 28, 2025 customer redline, QFL’s December 3, 2025 Amendment 2 draft, and Thornbury’s February 10, 2026 review form, which was never countersigned. [D034][D036][D038]
- Private records include Tobias’s packaging ownership/ramp note, the Zanesville visit, and Dana’s leave logistics. Their private context is material, particularly where ownership was not publicly announced. [D085][D087][D092]
- The North pipeline review has source metadata/path date **2025-09-12**, but its body says **Tuesday, September 16, 2025**, after Brackenwater’s handoff. Both dates are retained. [D079]

[D024][D027][D028]

### Marketing and use constraints

QFL’s signed MSA permits its marks only within its branded carrier portal. External press releases, case studies, and public customer lists require **prior written consent in each instance**. Customer feedback is licensed for product use under QFL’s MSA, but customer confidential information and data cannot be included in resulting product updates. ## ARTICLE 5. SUPPORT AND SERVICE LEVELS

**5.1 Support Tier Assignment.** During the active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall provide Customer with **Tier 2** Support Services for the Platform. Tier 2 Support Services are included in the annual subscription Fees set forth in Article 3 at no additional charge.

**5.2 Tier 2 Channels and Hours.** Under the Tier 2 support plan, Customer's designated system administrators (up to six (6) named individuals appointed by Customer's Director of Yard Operations) may submit support tickets via Pemberline's web-based support portal and by direct telephone hotline.
(a) **Severity 1 (Critical Yard Outage):** Telephone and portal support available twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year (24x7x365). A Severity 1 issue is defined as a complete inability of Authorized Users at one or more terminals to access the Platform, or a failure of core gate check-in or dock door assignment functions with no operational workaround, resulting in physical truck queues at terminal gates.
(b) **Severity 2 (Major Operational Degradation):** Support coverage available Monday through Saturday, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 2 issue is defined as a substantial impairment of primary features (such as yard jockey task dispatch latency, failure of EDI 214 status message transmission, or carrier portal booking failure) where core yard operations can continue via manual workaround within the Platform.
(c) **Severity 3 (Minor Feature Issue):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central Time, excluding US federal holidays. A Severity 3 issue is defined as a non-critical malfunction, reporting discrepancy, or user interface defect that has minimal impact on daily dock scheduling.
(d) **Severity 4 (Cosmetic or Inquiry):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 4 issue includes general "how-to" configuration questions, documentation requests, or cosmetic enhancement requests.

**5.3 Tier 2 Target Response Times.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline commits to the following initial human response times from the moment a ticket is logged in the support portal or received via the emergency telephone hotline:
* **Severity 1:** Within thirty (30) minutes, with continuous engineering engagement and status updates every sixty (60) minutes until service is restored.
* **Severity 2:** Within two (2) hours during covered hours, with status updates every four (4) hours.
* **Severity 3:** Within eight (8) business hours.
* **Severity 4:** Within two (2) business days.

**5.4 Platform Availability Commitment.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline shall maintain a Monthly Uptime Percentage for the production instance of the Platform of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%), measured across each calendar month. "Monthly Uptime Percentage" is calculated by subtracting from 100% the percentage of total minutes in the calendar month during which the Platform experienced Unscheduled Downtime.

**5.5 Exclusions from Unscheduled Downtime.** Unscheduled Downtime does not include unavailability resulting from: (a) Scheduled Maintenance windows occurring between Saturday 11:00 PM Central Time and Sunday 3:00 AM Central Time, provided Pemberline gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior electronic notice via the Platform status page; (b) Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 19.3; (c) failures of Customer's local yard Wi-Fi networks, cellular data terminals mounted in yard spotter cabs, barcode scanners, RFID gate readers, or local internet service providers; (d) interruptions caused by third-party transportation management systems (TMS) or warehouse management systems (WMS) integrated by Customer via API; or (e) suspension of Customer's access pursuant to Article 15.

**5.6 Service Credits.** If Pemberline fails to meet the 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage under the Tier 2 SLA in any given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit applied against its next invoice, calculated as a percentage of one-twelfth (1/12th) of the net annual subscription Fee ($18,993.33 USD monthly equivalent), as follows:
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 99.00% and 99.49%: Five percent (5%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 98.00% and 98.99%: Ten percent (10%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage below 98.00%: Twenty percent (20%) credit.
To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the Unscheduled Downtime occurred. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for any failure to meet the Tier 2 availability metrics, provided that if the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 97.00% for three (3) consecutive calendar months, Customer may treat such failure as a material breach under Section 16.2.
